text:
A: Alright? Gareth, Taunton.
B: Abena. Thornton Heath.
A: Nice to meet you. Sorry, you'll see a machine behind me. Home dialysis. I'm not hooked up, so no alarms, hopefully.
B: I saw. How long?
A: About three and a half years on dialysis. Five sessions a week, four hours each. Diagnosed at thirty-one, so, erm, it's been coming a while.
B: You do the needles yourself?
A: Yeah. Took a few months of training at the unit. My partner helps on bad days.
B: That's good. We have residents on dialysis at the hospital, three days a week, the transport takes them. They come back grey. Doing it at home is better. More control.
A: That's exactly why I wanted it. I like control. Bit of an engineer thing. Spreadsheet of my blood results, the lot.
B: [laughs] The Dutch man also has spreadsheets. You are the same.
A: We did get on, to be fair. Two engineers moaning about groundwater.
B: Mm. Your partner. She is your carer now?
A: Sort of, partly. She's a SENCo at a primary, works full-time, then comes home and helps me. I don't love that, if I'm honest. She didn't sign up for it.
B: Nobody signs up. But she stays. That means something.
A: Yeah. She does. We never got married, mind. Sana from Bolton told me to set a date.
B: [laughs] Sana tells everybody what to do. And I tell her to finish her course. So we are even.
A: [laughs] She offered to do Hannah's henna for free.
B: She would. She is kind. Talks too much, but kind. You are waiting for a kidney?
A: Two years on the list. My brother was tested, wasn't a match.
B: He wanted to?
A: [pause] Erm. He said he did. I'm not sure he was sorry when it came back no.
B: Hm. You can't make somebody give a kidney. But you can be upset. Both are true.
A: Yeah. Hadn't thought of it like that. Cheers.
B: You worked before?
A: Chartered civil engineer. Flood defences. Now I'm on benefits, which, you know, takes some getting used to. Went from the person everyone rang to the person filling in forms.
B: The forms are a job also. People think benefits is easy. You fill everything, they lose it, you fill again.
A: [laughs] I've got quite good at it, truth be told. Know which number to ring and what to say.
B: Good. Use it. It's your right. You paid in.
A: That's what Hannah says. What about you, long shifts?
B: Twelve hours, four or five days. Off today. Cooking light soup.
A: I'd kill for a proper bowl of soup. Too much potassium in most of it.
B: Then you can't have mine. It's tomatoes, goat, pepper. That's it.
A: [laughs] Probably for the best. Smells better than my freezer, I bet.
